newsitem.title: UK: Brent cash steady, Iraqi and Nigerian on the rise.
newsitem.headline: Brent cash steady, Iraqi and Nigerian on the rise.

text.p: Cash Brent spreads eased a little on Friday afternoon and North Sea differentials held on to recently established gains.
Traders said slow business had stalled Thursday's impetus on rising physical cargo differentials but that deltas could climb further next week.
"I'd expect to see diffs go up again next week but trade was too thin today to give much of a clue to direction," said a trader.
Two Oseberg cargoes traded at Dated Brent plus 13-15 cents and two Ekofisk at Dated Brent plus 15-17 cents.
The physical Brent market saw all four cargoes kept on Friday and differentials notionally unchanged at about 35 cents under June paper.
Dealers said good refining margins and arbitrage interest to the U.S. were helping support the market without yet boosting differentials further.
Prompt intermonth Brent spreads eased with a weaker outright market taking May/June to -14/-20 cents.
Nigerian crude, already sold out for May after heavy Asian purchases, got an extra filip from renewed ethnic disturbances which cut Forcados production by 90,000 barrels a day (bpd).
Bonny Light was valued at 45 cents, Qua Iboe at 40 cents and Forcados at +25 cents.
One of nine North Sea Flotta cargoes scheduled to load in May was cancelled on Friday.

The cancellation, for an end-May cargo, was for a 600,000 barrel loader and reduces the May Flotta programme to 4.85 million barrels from the originally planned 5.45 million barrels, down from 6.35 million expected to load in April.
Iraqi Kirkuk, valued at 25 cents over its May sales price of Brent -$2.20, continued to find plenty of buying interest, traders said.
